messages:
mika: quick sanity check on the new embeddings model 'synth-compact-v1' that landed on staging this morning. ran a small semantic-sim sweep on the wiki holdout (10k pairs). results look funky, asking for quick eyes.
priya: on it. which run id / quantization?
mika: run=synth-compact-v1/2026-03-20, default fp16. also tried int8-fast on a subset.
jorge: can you paste the recall@k numbers?
mika: sure — fp16 vs int8-fast (k=1,5,10)
```
Model           R@1    R@5    R@10   Silhouette
synth-compact-v1-fp16   0.732  0.892  0.918  0.41
synth-compact-v1-int8   0.691  0.867  0.900  0.37
baseline-sim-large      0.759  0.905  0.927  0.46
```
priya: int8 drop at R@1 ~4% absolute — expected but a bit higher than our usual quant penalty. silhouette drop also notable. did you do post-normalization?
mika: yes, all vectors l2-normalized before indexing. index is faiss.IndexIVFFlat with 1024 centroids. recall measured with exact knn (no ivf) for the table above to avoid index noise.
sam: did you check that tokenization/embedding pipeline is identical? small preproc diffs sometimes cause shifts.
mika: pipeline sha: a1b2c3, same tokenizer. logs show identical input shapes.
jorge: could be embedding scale — did you compare cosine distribution means?
mika: plotted cosine histograms. fp16 mean sim = 0.142, int8 mean sim = 0.131. variance slightly lower for int8. attached chart to the slack thread (uploaded).
priya: hunch: our int8 kernel uses per-channel scales that were tuned on next-token tasks, not embed distance. try symmetric quant with outlier-clipping and re-eval. also try applying a small temperature scaling on vectors (multiply by 1.03) before normalization as a quick probe.
mika: will try symmetric int8 + reclip. quick command I used:
```
python eval/sim_eval.py --model synth-compact-v1 --subset wiki-holdout --quant int8-fast --k 10 --norm l2 --out /tmp/synth_eval.json
```
eval-bot: model synth-compact-v1 (fp16) uploaded to staging at 2026-03-20T09:12:03Z. artifacts: s3://redwood-models/staging/synth-compact-v1/
deploy-bot: int8 artifact available at s3://redwood-models/staging/synth-compact-v1/int8-fast.tar.gz
sam: while you're re-running, also run the clustering purity test (labels=wiki-section) and the pairwise cosine delta for same-doc vs different-doc. that helps pinpoint whether within-doc neighbors drift more.
mika: noted. next runs: symmetric-int8, int8-reclip, and fp16 with temp-scale=1.03. will post new numbers by EOD.
priya: if recall doesn't recover, let's try a small re-calibration layer (single linear transform) trained on 50k pairs to align int8 outputs to fp16. cheap and often works.
jorge: also add a quick ANN baseline: build faiss HNSW index and measure R@10. sometimes IVFFlat centroid quantization masks the wins.
mika: ack. action items: (1) re-run symmetric int8 + reclip (2) run temp-scaling probe on fp16 & int8 (3) clustering purity + pairwise cosine deltas (4) HNSW vs IVFFlat compare. tagging @priya for calibration plan.
priya: thanks — ping me the eval artifacts. if we can get R@1 within 1.5% of fp16, OK for shipping as int8 default with note in release. :+1:
sam: great. also add a tiny failure-case set (20 hard pairs) to the PR so we can monitor regressions.
mika: will add to the repo and open PR with results + artifacts. thanks!
